problem: End-to-end seq2seq models on ALFRED (long-horizon, compositional navigation+manipulation with irreversible state changes) achieve very low success (~2-4%) in unseen rooms and appear to memorize training trajectories.
motivation: Household instructions are compositional and long, so the joint mapping from vision+language to low-level actions is hard to learn end to end and needs strictly aligned demonstrations. Decomposing into independently trainable perception, language and planning modules allows separate data and recovery strategies.
key_idea: Replace end-to-end learning with a modular pipeline (GCN-refined BEV mapping, BERT slot-filling language parsing, slot-conditioned LingUNet grounding, image-search disambiguation, rule-based A* planning) trained on separate vision and language data.
insight: Modularity greatly improves unseen-room success (37% vs 3% task success for the best seq2seq baseline), and the baseline reaches ~25% on training rooms, which suggests memorization. Giving the agent a perfect map raises task success from 37% to 60% while sub-goal success for PickUp/Put/Toggle barely changes, showing that map quality/positioning is the bottleneck for long tasks. Graph-convolution filtering raises per-cell map accuracy from ~55-65% to ~90-95% over raw projection.
method: Mapping: builds an egocentric BEV grid (0.25 m cells) from panorama RGB, segmentation and depth via geometric projection, summing competing class votes and averaging over rotations

GCN map refinement: grid-lattice graph (4-neighbour) with node features = n-class vectors, outputs 4 classes (unknown/navigable/target/obstacle), trained with NLL loss and SGD on ground-truth collision maps

Language understanding: BERT fine-tuned jointly for intent (navigation vs not) and 12-label slot filling on 1000 hand-labelled ALFRED instructions; also mines semantic object priors/knowledge graph from slot labels

Cross-modal grounding: LingUNet variant where slot-label embeddings become convolution kernels over ResNet features; trained on auto-generated synthetic referring data; output intersected with UNet instance segmentation
Disambiguation: downloads web images for unknown words and matches them to segmented regions by ResNet-feature cosine similarity (pixel or label comparison)
Planning: rule-based navigation and manipulation stacks with semantic object priors, A* with area-maximization heuristic to produce 13 low-level actions, and collision recovery

setting.backbone: BERT (fine-tuned) + GCN + LingUNet/ResNet + UNet segmentation, with rule-based A* planner
setting.training_data: 1000 hand-labelled instructions for BERT; GCN trained on scanned panoramas and GT collision maps of train rooms; LingUNet trained on auto-generated synthetic data; ALFRED living-room/bedroom subset (rooms 211-230, 311-330)
setting.observation: agent-acquired panorama RGB, depth (simulator-provided), instance segmentation (UNet)
setting.action_space: 13 discrete low-level AI2-THOR actions (MoveAhead, RotateRight, LookUp, Pickup, Put, Open, ToggleOn, ...) with object-name interaction instead of masks
setting.privileged: Simulator depth; the 'PerfectMap' variant additionally uses GT BEV maps

numbers.eval_set_note: Custom split: 20 held-out living rooms/bedrooms (301-310, 201-210), ~6000 instructions; not the official ALFRED unseen split
numbers.extra: Custom train/test split; baselines retrained on remaining 40 rooms

numbers.eval_set_note: Custom 20 held-out rooms, same as main
numbers.evidence: Table 1 and Table 2, MoViLan + PerfectMap rows

numbers_note: Split is the authors' custom room split, so numbers are not comparable to the official ALFRED leaderboard. Percentages are rounded by the paper; PLW = path-length-weighted values shown in parentheses.
results: On the custom unseen-room split MoViLan attains 37% task and 45% goal-condition success versus 3% and 4% for SEQ2SEQ+PM. With perfect maps it reaches 60%/72%. Sub-goal rates are also higher (e.g. GoTo 45 vs 31).
limitations: Evaluated on a self-defined, easier-to-control subset of ALFRED (living rooms and bedrooms only), not the official split, so comparisons are not standard
Depends on hand-crafted rules, simulator-provided depth, panorama scanning and hand-labelled slot data; planning is rule-based with no learned closed loop
Interaction uses object names rather than pixel masks, unlike the baseline, and the mapping accuracy limits performance (PerfectMap gap)
